 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao

Judgment:

entities.text:
National Insurance Company ... vs Vijjala Sambasiva Rao
And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant is 3rd respondent/Insurance company and the respondents are claim petitioner and 1st respondent in M.O.P.No.112 of 2005 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-VIII Additional District Judge (Fast Track Court), Visakhapatnam.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-VIII Additional District Judge (Fast Track Court), Visakhapatnam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant filed the appeal questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal.
2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim petition.

3. The claim petitioner filed the petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 read with Rule 455 of the A.P.M.V. Rules, 1989 against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident that took place on 25.10.2004.
VGKR,J 4.

The brief averments in the petition filed by the petitioner are as follows:
On 25.10.2004 at about 4.30 p.m. the petitioner was going on his scooter bearing registration No.AP 31A 5506 from Visakhapatnam to S.Kota and when he reached Gangupudi Shandy, a car bearing registration No.AP 31W 9086 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at high speed without blowing horn came in opposite direction and dashed against the scooter of the petitioner
, due to that, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

The S.H.O., L.Kota P.S.
registered a case in crime No.47 of 2004 against the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under Sections 337, 338 and 279 of IPC.

The 1st respondent is driver, the 2nd respondent is owner and the 3rd respondent is insurer of the offending car, hence, all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
VGKR,J 5.
The 1st respondent was set ex parte.
Respondent Nos.2 and 3 filed counters separately by denying the manner of accident, age, avocation and income of the petitioner.

It is pleaded by the 3rd respondent/Insurance company that the accident occurred due to negligence of the petitioner, the claim of the petitioner is very excessive, and the driver of the offending car was not holding valid The National Insurance Company ... vs Vijjala Sambasiva Rao And 2 Others on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20213361/
1 and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

sentences.text:
6. Based on the above pleadings of both the parties, the following issues were settled for trial by the Tribunal:
1) Whether the pleaded accident occurred on account of the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle (Indica car) bearing reg.No.AP 31W 9086 by its driver and whether it resulted injuries to the petitioner?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and from which of the respondents?
3) To what extent?
7.
During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioner, P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A.1 to A.13 VGKR,J were marked.
On behalf of the respondents, no oral or documentary evidence was adduced.

8. At the culmination of the enquiry, after considering the evidence on record and on appreciation of the same, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the accident occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car and accordingly, allowed the claim petition and granted a sum of Rs.2,08,250/- towards compensation to the petitioner with costs and interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of payment against all the respondents.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the 3rd respondent/Insurance company has preferred the present appeal.

9. Heard Sri Venkateswarlu Paladugu, learned counsel for the appellant/3rd respondent-Insuance company, and Sri Jayanthi S.C. Sekhar, learned counsel for the 1st respondent/petitioner and perused the record.
VGKR,J 10.

Now, the point for determination is:
Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference, if so, to what extent?
11. POINT:
In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1.
The petitioner reiterated the contents of the claim petition in his chief examination affidavit.
As seen from Ex.A.3-attested copy of charge sheet, charge sheet was filed against the rider of the scooter i.e., the petitioner and the driver of the car i.e., the 1 st respondent.
On perusal of the entire documentary evidence, it is proved that the accident in question occurred due to composite negligence on the part of the petitioner and on the part of the 1st respondent.

sentences.text: Coming to the compensation, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,08,250/- to the petitioner.

On considering that the petitioner could not be able to attend his duties for about six VGKR,J months, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.7,500/- towards loss of earnings for a period of six months @ Rs.1,250/- p.m..
13.
On considering the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.1,000/- towards transport charges.

On considering Exs.A.5 to A.8-medical bills for a total sum of Rs.72,613/-
coupled with the evidence of P.W.2-Doctor, who treated the petitioner, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.80,000/- towards medical expenses and extra nourishment.
Since the petitioner sustained severe injuries, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.5,000/- towards pain and suffering.

14. Coming to the disability sustained by the petitioner, the material on record reveals that the petitioner is suffering with disability of 45% which is permanent in nature which is supported by Ex.A.10-disability certificate issued by P.W.2 and Ex.A.11-case sheet.

On considering the documentary evidence, the Tribunal fixed the age of the petitioner as 30 years and also his annual income as VGKR,J Rs.15,000/- and accordingly, awarded an amount of Rs.1,14,750/- towards 45%
disability sustained by the petitioner.
15. In total, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.2,08,250/- towards compensation.

Since the petitioner sustained severe grievous injuries and also suffered 45% disability and he took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, in my view, is just and reasonable, hence, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal in awarding the quantum of compensation.

16. Since it is proved that the accident occurred by reason of composite negligence on the part of the petitioner/rider of the scooter and the 1st respondent/driver of the car involved in the accident and on considering the overall circumstances of the case, 25% contributory negligence is fixed on the rider of the scooter/petitioner and 75% contributory negligence is fixed on the driver of the car/1st respondent.

As such, the petitioner is entitled to VGKR,J compensation of Rs.1,56,187/-
(Rs.2,08,250/- - Rs.52,063/-).
The 1st respondent is driver and agent of the 2nd respondent.
It is not in dispute that the offending car of the 2nd respondent was insured with the 3rd respondent/Insurance company and the policy was also in force as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the 3rd respondent being the insurer of the offending car has to indemnify the 2 nd respondent and is liable to pay the compensation of Rs.1,56,187/- with proportionate costs and interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of payment.
17. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed.
The order of the Tribunal is modified by reducing the compensation of Rs.2,08,250/- awarded by the Tribunal to Rs.1,56,187/-.

The appellant/3rd respondent-Insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount, after deducting the deposited amount, if any, along with proportionate costs and interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of payment, before the Tribunal within two months from the date of this judgment.
The order of the VGKR,J Tribunal in all other respects shall remain intact.
No order as to costs.
